question: What is an NTN?
variants: What does NTN mean? | NTN number kya hai? | Is CNIC my NTN? | Does a company get an NTN? | NTN aur CNIC same hote hain? | ntn | national tax number | tax number | tax id | ntn kya hai | ntn number kya hota hai | cnic ntn | cnic same as ntn | 13 digit ntn | 7 digit ntn | Explain NTN in simple words | NTN ka matlab kya hota hai | Ye NTN kya cheez hai | NTN kis ko kehte hain | meaning of NTN number | what is national tax number in Pakistan | ntn kia hy | ntn kya hy | ntn mean | whts ntn | tax number kya hota hai | NTN samajh nahi aata | what is a tax identification number FBR
answer_en: NTN means National Tax Number, which is your tax ID number from FBR (Federal Board of Revenue), just as your CNIC identifies you as a citizen. If you earn money from a job, business, or freelancing and want to file an income tax return, you generally need to be registered with FBR, and you can e-enrol through FBR's online portal IRIS. For an individual, your 13-digit CNIC number is used as your NTN/Registration Number, while a company or AOP (such as a partnership) gets a separate 7-digit NTN from FBR after e-enrolment. For the latest rules, please check fbr.gov.pk.
answer_ur: NTN ka matlab hai National Tax Number, yani FBR (Federal Board of Revenue) ka diya hua tax ID number, jaise CNIC aapko shehri batata hai waise NTN aapko taxpayer batata hai. Agar aap job, business ya freelancing se paise kamate hain aur income tax return file karna chahte hain, to aam taur par FBR mein registered hona zaroori hota hai, aur aap FBR ke online portal IRIS par e-enrol kar sakte hain. Individual ke liye 13 digit CNIC number hi NTN/Registration Number hota hai, jabke company ya AOP (partnership jaisa group) ko e-enrolment ke baad FBR alag 7 digit NTN deta hai. Taaza tareen rules ke liye fbr.gov.pk check karein.
source_line: Based on FBR Register for Income Tax page (fbr.gov.pk). FBR helpline: 051-111-772-772

answer_en: You may need an NTN if you are required to file an income tax return, or if you want to register as a taxpayer with FBR; this can include salaried people, business owners, freelancers, property owners, and companies, depending on their income and situation. Companies are required to file an income tax return, and AOPs (such as partnerships) may be required to file if they meet the legal conditions. Once you obtain an NTN, you are generally required to file an income tax return every year, even if no tax is payable. You can also register voluntarily to become a filer, and non-filers may face higher withholding tax on certain transactions, so confirm the current rules with FBR. Whether you must pay tax depends on your income and the rules for that tax year, which can change, so check fbr.gov.pk for the latest information.
answer_ur: Aapko NTN ki zaroorat ho sakti hai agar aap income tax return file karne ke liye required hain, ya agar aap FBR mein taxpayer/filer banna chahte hain; is mein job karne wale, business karne wale, freelancers, property owners aur companies shamil ho sakti hain, lekin yeh unki income aur situation par depend karta hai. Companies ko income tax return file karna zaroori hai, aur AOPs (partnership jaise groups) ko return file karna zaroori ho sakta hai agar woh legal conditions meet karte hain. Jab aap NTN le lete hain to aam taur par aapko har saal income tax return file karna hota hai, chahe tax na banta ho. Aap apni marzi se bhi register kar sakte hain agar filer banna chahte hain, aur non-filers ko kuch transactions par zyada withholding tax lag sakta hai, is liye current rules FBR se confirm karein. Tax dena hai ya nahi yeh aapki income aur us saal ke rules par depend karta hai, jo change ho sakte hain, is liye taaza maloomat ke liye fbr.gov.pk check karein.
source_line: Based on Section 114, Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 (fbr.gov.pk). FBR helpline: 051-111-772-772

question: How do I register for an NTN online?
variants: How to register for NTN online? | How to make an NTN? | NTN kaise banta hai? | NTN registration ka tareeqa batao | How to apply for NTN online | NTN online kaise banayein | NTN kaise banta hai | NTN registration process step by step | Steps to get NTN through IRIS | how to get tax number from mobile | I want to become a taxpayer where do I begin | taxpayer banne ke liye kahan se start karun | NTN ka online process kya hai | ntn banao | ntn apply online | ntn registration | how to make ntn | ntn bnana hy | e-enrolment kaise karein | how to e-enrol with FBR | internet se NTN kaise milega | get ntn from home online
answer_en: If you are an individual, you can register for an NTN online through FBR's IRIS portal at iris.fbr.gov.pk, but online registration is for income tax only and is not available for companies or AOPs (such as partnerships). Before you start, read FBR's User Guide and keep ready a computer or laptop, internet, a scanner, a mobile SIM registered against your own CNIC, your own personal email address, and a scanned PDF of the certificate for a personal bank account in your own name; if you have a business, also keep a scanned PDF of proof of rent or ownership of the business premises and a paid utility bill not older than 3 months. Open IRIS, start registration as an individual, enter your details such as CNIC, mobile number, and email address, upload the scanned documents, submit the form, and complete any verification FBR asks for. After registration, your 13-digit CNIC is used as your NTN/Registration Number and you can use it to log in to IRIS. A company or AOP cannot register online, so its principal officer must visit a Tax House Facilitation Counter or RTO with the required original documents.
answer_ur: Agar aap individual hain to aap FBR ke IRIS portal iris.fbr.gov.pk par online NTN register kar sakte hain, lekin online registration sirf income tax ke liye hai aur company ya AOP (partnership) online register nahi kar sakte. Shuru karne se pehle FBR ki User Guide parh lein aur computer ya laptop, internet, scanner, apne CNIC par registered SIM wala mobile, apna personal email address, aur apne naam ke personal bank account ke certificate ki scanned PDF tayyar rakhein; agar business hai to premises ke kiraye ya malkiyat ka saboot aur 3 mahine se purana na hone wala paid utility bill bhi scanned PDF mein rakhein. IRIS kholein, individual ke taur par registration shuru karein, CNIC, mobile number aur email jaisi details bharein, scanned documents upload karein, form submit karein aur FBR ki mangi hui verification mukammal karein. Registration ke baad aapka 13 digit CNIC aapka NTN/Registration Number hota hai jis se aap IRIS mein login kar sakte hain. Company ya AOP online register nahi kar sakte, un ke principal officer ko zaroori original documents ke sath Tax House Facilitation Counter ya RTO jana hota hai.
source_line: Based on FBR Register for Income Tax and IRIS registration pages (fbr.gov.pk). FBR helpline: 051-111-772-772

question: What documents are needed for NTN registration?
variants: What documents are required for NTN? | What do I need to register for an NTN? | NTN ke liye kaunse documents chahiye? | NTN banwane ke liye kya kya chahiye? | Which documents are required for NTN? | What papers are needed to apply for NTN? | NTN ke liye kaun se documents chahiye | NTN banwane ke liye kya kya lagta hai | NTN ke kaghzat | documents required for tax registration | CNIC copy and bill needed for NTN | ntn documents | ntn papers | ntn requirements | ntn ke liye kya chahiye | ntn banane ka saman | Do I need a utility bill for NTN registration | bank statement needed for NTN? | what to keep ready before NTN application | ntn kagzaat | required documents ntn registration | utility bill or bank statement needed for registration | ntn docs | ntn docs kya hain
answer_en: The documents depend on whether you register as an individual, an AOP (such as a partnership), or a company. An individual registering online needs a CNIC, NICOP, or passport number, a mobile number in use, an active personal email address, and a scanned PDF of a personal bank-account certificate in their own name, and may also be asked for nationality, residential address, accounting period, and details of salary, business, or property income; if you have a business, add proof of rent or ownership of the premises and a paid utility bill not older than 3 months, and bring originals if you register in person at a Tax House. An AOP's authorized partner must visit a Tax House Facilitation Counter with the original partnership deed (plus the Registrar of Firms certificate if the firm is registered), CNICs of all partners, an original authorization letter signed by all partners, a SIM in the partner's own name not already registered with FBR, an AOP email address, and an AOP bank-account certificate. A company's Principal Officer must visit a Tax House Facilitation Counter with the incorporation certificate, CNICs of all directors, details of every major shareholder holding 10% or more shares, an original letter signed by all directors authorizing the Principal Officer, a SIM in the Principal Officer's own name not already registered with FBR, a company email address, and a company bank-account certificate. An AOP or company that has a business also needs proof of rent or ownership of the premises and a paid utility bill not older than 3 months.
answer_ur: Documents is baat par depend karte hain ke aap individual, AOP (partnership) ya company ke taur par register ho rahe hain. Individual ko online registration ke liye CNIC, NICOP ya passport number, istemal mein mobile number, active personal email address, aur apne naam ke personal bank account certificate ki scanned PDF chahiye, aur nationality, residential address, accounting period, aur salary, business ya property income ki details bhi mangi ja sakti hain; business ho to premises ke kiraye ya malkiyat ka saboot aur 3 mahine se purana na hone wala paid utility bill bhi chahiye, aur Tax House mein khud register karte waqt original documents le jayein. AOP ke mukhtar partner ko Tax House Facilitation Counter par original partnership deed (registered firm ho to Registrar of Firms ka certificate bhi), tamam partners ke CNIC, tamam partners ke dastkhat wala original authorization letter, apne naam par registered aur FBR mein pehle se registered na hone wali SIM, AOP ka email address aur AOP ke naam ka bank account certificate le kar jana hota hai. Company ke Principal Officer ko Tax House Facilitation Counter par incorporation certificate, tamam directors ke CNIC, 10% ya zyada shares rakhne wale har major shareholder ki details, tamam directors ke dastkhat wala original authorization letter, apne naam par registered aur FBR mein pehle se registered na hone wali SIM, company ka email address aur company ke naam ka bank account certificate le kar jana hota hai. Agar AOP ya company ka business hai to premises ke kiraye ya malkiyat ka saboot aur 3 mahine se purana na hone wala paid utility bill bhi chahiye.
source_line: Based on FBR Register for Income Tax page (fbr.gov.pk); check the live page for the exact document list. FBR helpline: 051-111-772-772

question: What is FBR IRIS?
variants: What is IRIS? | What is FBR IRIS portal? | IRIS kya hai? | FBR IRIS kya hota hai? | iris | iris 2 | iris 2.0 | iris portal | fbr iris | iris portal kya hai | iris account kya hota hai | file return online | online tax return | e-filing | psid | taxpayer verification | What does IRIS mean? | Explain FBR IRIS portal | IRIS portal kya hota hai | IRIS kis kaam aata hai | What is the FBR website for filing tax returns | tax filing website Pakistan kaunsi hai | FBR portal for taxpayers | iris kia hy | iris kya hy | iris fbr | what is iris portal used for | Pakistan ka tax return portal | online portal to file taxes in Pakistan | which site do taxpayers use in Pakistan
answer_en: IRIS is FBR's official online tax portal at iris.fbr.gov.pk, and its full name is IRIS 2.0. You can use it to register for an NTN, log in to your FBR tax account, and file your income tax return online, with a simplified income tax form, income and wealth statements, and e-filing. To log in, use the Registration Number/NTN and password you receive when you register with FBR; for an individual, the 13-digit CNIC is used as the NTN/Registration Number. IRIS is not only for income tax, as it also offers tax-payment slips (PSID), taxpayer verification, and certain sales-tax services. Always use the official address iris.fbr.gov.pk and never share your IRIS password, OTP, or CNIC details with anyone.
answer_ur: IRIS FBR ka official online tax portal hai, iris.fbr.gov.pk, aur iska poora naam IRIS 2.0 hai. Is par aap NTN ke liye register kar sakte hain, apne FBR tax account mein login kar sakte hain, aur income tax return online file kar sakte hain, jis mein simplified income tax form, income aur wealth statements, aur e-filing shamil hain. Login ke liye registration ke waqt milne wala Registration Number/NTN aur password use karein, aur individual ke liye 13 digit CNIC hi NTN/Registration Number hota hai. IRIS sirf income tax ke liye nahi hai, is par tax payment slip (PSID), taxpayer verification aur kuch sales tax services bhi hain. Hamesha official address iris.fbr.gov.pk use karein aur apna IRIS password, OTP ya CNIC details kisi ke sath share na karein.
source_line: Based on FBR and the IRIS portal (fbr.gov.pk, iris.fbr.gov.pk). FBR helpline: 051-111-772-772

answer_en: To log in, type iris.fbr.gov.pk into your browser, enter your 13-digit CNIC without dashes in the Registration No. field if you are an individual (or your 7-digit NTN if you are a company or AOP), enter your password, and select Login. If you forgot your password, choose Forgot Password on the IRIS login page only if you still have access to both the email address and mobile number registered with FBR, then follow the on-screen instructions to verify your identity and create a new password. If you no longer have access to your registered mobile number or email, choose Account Recovery and follow the instructions to update the mobile number registered against your CNIC. If Account Recovery is not available, visit your nearest Regional Tax Office (RTO) with your original CNIC and the required documents, and call the FBR helpline 051-111-772-772 for general help. Use only iris.fbr.gov.pk and never share your password, OTP, or verification code with anyone.

answer_en: FBR provides two ways to change your income-tax registration details. In IRIS, file Registration Form 181 (Form of Registration filed for modification) to update your mobile number, personal or residential address, business address, addition of a business branch, legal representative, or bank account, and FBR may approve or refuse the modification after reviewing the form and making any necessary inquiry. For your email address, CNIC number, Pakistan Origin Card (POC) details, discontinuance of business, jurisdiction for income-tax return assessment, or deregistration, visit your relevant Regional Tax Office (RTO) with the required documents. If Form 181 or the online option does not work, call the FBR helpline 051-111-772-772.

IRIS mein Registration Form 181 (Form of Registration filed for modification) file kar ke aap mobile number, personal ya residential address, business address, business ki nayi branch, legal representative ya bank account badal sakte hain, aur FBR form review kar ke, zaroori inquiry ke baad, modification approve ya refuse kar sakta hai. answer_en: FBR's official registration pages do not list a fee for registering for an NTN, and you can register directly through FBR's IRIS portal at iris.fbr.gov.pk. You do not need to pay an agent or consultant to obtain an NTN, although a tax consultant you hire may charge their own service fee, which is separate from FBR. answer_ur: FBR ki official registration pages mein NTN register karne ki koi fee list nahi ki gayi, aur aap seedha IRIS portal iris.fbr.gov.pk par register kar sakte hain. question: Who must file an income tax return?
variants: Who has to file a tax return? | Who must file income tax return in Pakistan? | Is it compulsory to file a tax return? | Tax return kis ko file karna chahiye? | Tax return file karna kis par zaroori hai? | Who is required to submit an income tax return? | Kis ko tax return file karna zaroori hai | Kon log return file karte hain | Return file karna kis par lazmi hai | do salaried people need to file tax return | Do I have to file a return if I earn a salary | tax return kis ko bharna chahiye | return kon file kare | who files income tax return | filing return mandatory kis ke liye | return bharna lazmi hai kya | salary wale ko return file karna hai? | kya main return file karun | must I submit tax return as employee | filing obligation for individuals Pakistan | Which people are obliged to file income tax return | legally kis par return file karna lazmi hai
answer_en: Under Section 114 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, you may have to file an income tax return if any one of several conditions applies, so you do not need to meet all of them. These include being a company or a non-profit organization, having taxable income above the applicable yearly threshold, having an NTN, or having business income above the applicable threshold. They also include owning immovable property of 500 square yards or more or a flat with 2,000 square feet or more covered area in a rating area, owning a motor vehicle with engine capacity above 1,000 cc, and having a commercial or industrial electricity connection with an annual bill above Rs. 500,000. Being a member of a chamber of commerce, trade association, market committee, or professional body, or having paid income tax in either of the last two tax years, can also make filing necessary. The law also contains exceptions and thresholds can change, so check fbr.gov.pk or call the FBR helpline 051-111-772-772 for your own situation.
answer_ur: Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 ki Section 114 ke mutabiq agar kai conditions mein se koi aik bhi aap par lagu ho to aapko income tax return file karna par sakta hai, saari conditions poori hona zaroori nahi. In mein company ya non-profit organization hona, taxable income yearly threshold se zyada hona, NTN hona, ya business income threshold se zyada hona shamil hai. Rating area mein 500 square yards ya zyada immovable property ya 2,000 square feet ya zyada covered area wala flat, 1,000 cc se zyada engine capacity wali motor vehicle, aur Rs. 500,000 se zyada salana bill wala commercial ya industrial bijli ka connection bhi conditions hain. Chamber of commerce, trade association, market committee ya professional body ka member hona, ya pichle do tax years mein se kisi mein income tax dena bhi filing zaroori bana sakta hai. Law mein exceptions bhi hain aur thresholds change ho sakti hain, is liye apne case ke liye fbr.gov.pk dekhein ya FBR helpline 051-111-772-772 par rabta karein.
source_line: Based on FBR return-filing and ATL pages and Section 114, Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 (fbr.gov.pk); thresholds depend on the current Finance Act. FBR helpline: 051-111-772-772

question: What is the deadline for filing a return?
variants: What is the last date to file income tax return? | When is the tax return deadline? | Tax return ki last date kya hai? | Return kab tak file karna hai? | tax return deadline | last date tax return | return last date | income tax return due date | return kab tak file karna | tax return ki last date | return deadline kab hai | deadline extension | last date extend | return date barhi | company return deadline | AOP return deadline | special tax year deadline | tax year 2026 | tax year 2027 | When is the last date to submit tax return? | Return filing due date kab hai | Tax return kab tak jama karwana hai | Return ki akhri tareekh kya hai | Return file karne ki akhri date | What date is the tax return due | by when should I file my return | last date for tax year filing | return due date | return akhri tareekh | akhri date return | filing deadline kya hai | tax return last date kab hai | until when can I file tax return without penalty | kab tak return file kar sakte hain bina jurmane ke | due date income tax filing Pakistan | until which date can I file this tax year | kis date tak return file kar sakte hain tax year ke liye
answer_en: The normal income tax return deadline is 30 September each year for individuals and AOPs (such as partnerships), 31 December each year for companies, and 30 September each year for companies with a special tax year. A return relates to a tax year that normally runs from 1 July to 30 June, so Tax Year 2026 covers July 2025 to June 2026. FBR can extend the deadline, and for Tax Year 2026 it extended the deadline for persons originally due on 30 September first to 15 October 2026 and then to 31 October 2026. Because extension dates can change every year, check the latest notice on fbr.gov.pk before filing. Beware of fake notices and trust only official FBR notices on fbr.gov.pk.
answer_ur: Income tax return ki aam last date individuals aur AOPs (partnership jaise groups) ke liye har saal 30 September, companies ke liye har saal 31 December, aur special tax year wali companies ke liye har saal 30 September hai. Return aik tax year ka hota hai jo aam taur par 1 July se 30 June tak hota hai, maslan Tax Year 2026 July 2025 se June 2026 tak ka period hai. FBR deadline barha sakta hai, aur Tax Year 2026 ke liye jin ki date 30 September thi unhein pehle 15 October 2026 aur phir 31 October 2026 tak extension di gayi. Extension har saal change ho sakti hai, is liye file karne se pehle fbr.gov.pk par taaza notice dekhein. Jaali notices se bachein aur sirf fbr.gov.pk par FBR ke official notices par bharosa karein.

question: What is a filer vs a non-filer?
variants: What is a non-filer? | What is the difference between filer and non-filer? | Filer aur non-filer mein kya farq hai? | Non-filer kaun hota hai? | non filer | ATL | active taxpayer | non filer kya hota hai | filer aur non filer ka farq | filer kise kehte hain | ATL kya hai | ATL status | 9966 | nil return filer | NTN filer | return file karne ke baad filer | filer tax | non filer tax | filer non filer tax rate | Difference between filer and non-filer | What does filer mean? | Filer aur non filer mein kya farq hai | Non filer kise kehte hain | Filer kya hota hai | who is a non-filer | filer meaning | filer vs non filer | non filer kon hai | filer non-filer farq | what makes someone a filer in Pakistan | ATL mein hona ya na hona kya farq dalta hai | filer ka matlab | non filer ka matlab | Why is it better to be on filer list | filer list mein hona kyun behtar hai
answer_en: A filer is a person whose name appears on FBR's Active Taxpayer List (ATL), which generally happens after you file your income tax return through IRIS, while a non-filer is anyone not on the ATL, including people who never registered with FBR and registered people who have not filed a return. Filers generally face lower withholding tax on certain transactions such as bank transactions, property transactions, and vehicle registration, while non-filers generally face higher rates that change with each Finance Act or budget. Having an NTN does not automatically make you a filer, and a nil return can still count, so if your income is below the taxable limit, filing a nil return can help you appear on the ATL, but confirm your own position with FBR. To check, use FBR's online ATL status check, send an SMS in the format ATL [space] your 13-digit CNIC to 9966 (for a company or AOP use ATL [space] 7-digit NTN), or download the ATL from FBR's website. For the latest rules and rates, please check fbr.gov.pk.
answer_ur: Filer woh shakhs hai jis ka naam FBR ki Active Taxpayer List (ATL) mein hota hai, jo aam taur par IRIS par income tax return file karne ke baad hota hai, jabke non-filer woh hai jo ATL mein nahi hota, yani jis ne registration nahi ki ya registered hai magar return file nahi kiya. Filers ko aam taur par bank transactions, property aur vehicle registration jaisay kaamon par kam withholding tax lagta hai, aur non-filers ko zyada rate lagte hain jo har Finance Act/budget ke sath badalte hain. NTN hone se aap filer nahi ban jate, aur nil return bhi count ho sakti hai, yani income tax limit se kam ho to nil return file karne se aap ATL mein aa sakte hain, lekin apne case ke liye FBR se confirm karein. Check karne ke liye FBR ki website par ATL status dekhein, SMS mein ATL [space] apna 13 digit CNIC likh kar 9966 par bhejein (company ya AOP ke liye ATL [space] 7 digit NTN), ya FBR ki website se ATL download karein. Taaza tareen rules aur rates ke liye fbr.gov.pk check karein.

question: What are the benefits of being a filer?
variants: Is it good to be on the ATL? | Filer kyun banna chahiye? | Filer banne ke fayde kya hain? | ATL mein aane ka kya faida hai? | benefits of filer | filer benefits | filer ke fayde | filer banne ke fayde | ATL benefits | filer non filer tax difference | filer tax benefits | property tax filer | vehicle tax filer | bank cash withdrawal filer | dividend filer | shares capital gains filer | prize bond filer | ATL faida | active taxpayer benefits | Why should I become a filer? | Benefits of filing tax return | Filer banne ke fayde | What do I gain from being a filer | Filer hone ke kya faide hain | advantages of being on active taxpayer list | filer benefit | filer ke fawaid | filer rate lower tax deduction benefit | become filer advantages | filer banne se kya milta hai | lower withholding tax for filers | kya filer banna acha hai | why file return Pakistan benefits
answer_en: The main benefit is that filers generally pay lower withholding tax than non-filers on many everyday money matters. FBR says being on the Active Taxpayer List (ATL) gives lower tax deducted by banks on profits and cash withdrawals, reduced withholding tax when registering or transferring a motor vehicle, lower tax when buying or selling property, lower withholding tax on capital gains from selling securities such as shares, lower tax on dividends, lower withholding tax on prize bond winnings, and the ability to claim back tax that was withheld in excess. Tax guides also mention that a tax record may help with loans, business contracts, or visa applications, but FBR does not list this as an ATL benefit, so treat it as a possible general benefit and not a guarantee. Being a non-filer is not illegal, and a non-filer can still buy property, open a bank account, and register a vehicle, but may pay higher withholding tax on those transactions. Current filer and non-filer rates change with the budget, so check FBR's Withholding Tax Rate Card on fbr.gov.pk.
answer_ur: Filer hone ka sab se bara faida yeh hai ke aam taur par non-filer ke muqable mein rozmarra ke kai paison ke maamlaat par kam withholding tax dena parta hai. FBR ke mutabiq Active Taxpayer List (ATL) mein hone se bank profits aur cash withdrawal par kam tax deduction, gaari register ya transfer karwate waqt kam withholding tax, property khareedne ya bechne par kam tax, shares jaisi securities ke capital gain par kam withholding tax, dividend par kam tax, prize bond winning par kam withholding tax, aur zyada kate hue tax ko claim back karne ki sahulat milti hai. Tax guides loan, business contract ya visa ke liye tax record ko madadgar bhi batate hain, lekin FBR ne yeh ATL ke faydon mein nahi likha, is liye ise aam taur par madadgar ho sakta hai samjhein, guarantee nahi. Non-filer hona qanooni jurm nahi hai, non-filer property khareed sakta hai, bank account khol sakta hai aur gaari register karwa sakta hai, lekin in transactions par zyada withholding tax lag sakta hai. Filer aur non-filer ke current rates budget ke sath badalte hain, is liye fbr.gov.pk par Withholding Tax Rate Card dekhein.

question: How do I file a return on IRIS, step by step?
variants: How to file income tax return on IRIS? | How to file tax return online in Pakistan? | Step by step tax return filing | Tax return kaise file karte hain? | IRIS par return kaise file karein? | file income tax return | file tax return online | IRIS return filing | how to file return on IRIS | income tax return kaise file karte hain | tax return step by step | IRIS CNIC login | Declaration | 114(1) | 114(I) | normal return | salaried return | salary return | simplified salary return | Tax Asaan | FBR video tutorial | IRIS help | How to file income tax return on IRIS | IRIS par return kaise file karte hain | Step by step return filing guide | Explain the process of submitting a return on IRIS | how do I submit my return online | return file karne ka tareeqa | online return filing process Pakistan | file return iris | return filing steps | return kaise file karein | tax return kaise bharte hain | iris return process | submit return on FBR portal | guide to e-filing return | how to do e filing FBR | return bharne ka tareeqa step by step | IRIS return filing ka method
answer_en: Before you start, keep ready your CNIC and IRIS password (first-time filers must register with FBR first), income details such as a salary certificate, tax deduction certificates showing tax already withheld, bank details, and details of assets such as property or vehicles if applicable. Open iris.fbr.gov.pk and log in (for an individual Pakistani the user ID is the 13-digit CNIC without dashes, while companies and AOPs use their 7-digit NTN), click Declaration or the File Your Income Tax Return quick link, choose Returns/Statements (Original) and then Normal Return (Ind/AOP/COY), select the tax period, and click Continue. Fill in your income in the relevant sections (salary under Employment, and business, freelance, rental, and other income in the applicable sections), enter tax already paid or deducted, and use Calculate where the form provides it. Then complete the Wealth Statement, because FBR says both the Return of Income and Wealth Statement must be completed for a successful online return, verify the declaration with your 4-digit eFBR PIN, click Submit and confirm, and save or print the acknowledgement PDF once both forms move from Draft to Completed Task. Later check that your name appears on the Active Taxpayer List (ATL); if your income is only from salary and other sources and salary is more than 50% of your total income, FBR provides a simplified Declaration form 114(I), and if your income or assets are complicated consider help from a registered tax adviser.
answer_ur: Shuru karne se pehle apna CNIC aur IRIS password (pehli baar return file karne walon ko pehle FBR mein register hona zaroori hai), income ki details jaise salary certificate, tax deduction certificates jin mein employer ya bank ka kata hua tax likha ho, bank details, aur lagu ho to property ya gaariyon ki details tayyar rakhein. iris.fbr.gov.pk kholein aur login karein (Pakistani individual ke liye 13 digit CNIC bina dashes ke, company aur AOP ke liye 7 digit NTN), Declaration ya File Your Income Tax Return quick link par click karein, Returns/Statements (Original) aur phir Normal Return (Ind/AOP/COY) chunein, tax period select kar ke Continue karein. Income relevant sections mein darj karein (salary Employment mein, business, freelance, kiraya aur doosri income mutaliqa sections mein), pehle se kata hua ya ada shuda tax likhein, aur Calculate ka option ho to use karein. Phir Wealth Statement complete karein kyunke FBR ke mutabiq online return ke liye Return of Income aur Wealth Statement dono zaroori hain, 4 digit eFBR PIN se declaration verify karein, Submit kar ke confirm karein, aur jab dono Draft se Completed Task mein chale jayein to acknowledgement PDF save ya print kar lein. Baad mein ATL mein apna naam check karein; agar income sirf salary aur doosre sources se ho aur salary total income ka 50% se zyada ho to FBR simplified Declaration form 114(I) deta hai, aur income ya assets complicated hon to registered tax adviser se madad lein.

question: What is the penalty for filing late?
variants: What is the penalty for late tax return? | What happens if I file my tax return late? | What if I miss the tax return deadline? | Late return file karne par kitna jurmana hai? | Deadline miss ho jaye to kya hota hai? | late return penalty | penalty for late tax return | late return jurmana | late filing fine | miss tax return deadline | section 182 penalty | section 182A | ATL mein wapas aana | ATL-U undertaking | IRIS ATL undertaking | file late return | late filer ATL | What is the fine for late filing of tax return? | How much penalty if I file after due date | Late return par kitna jurmana lagta hai | Der se return file karne ki saza | Return late file karun to kya hoga | Penalty for submitting return after deadline | late filing jurmana | late return fine | jurmana late return | late return par fine kitna | fine for filing after last date | late file penalty amount Pakistan | kitna fine lagega agar return late ho | penalty late filers FBR | late filing ki saza | How much fine for returning late after due date | due date ke baad return dene par kitna fine
answer_en: You can usually still file a late income tax return, but late filing can lead to two separate charges. The Section 182 late-filing penalty is 0.1% of the tax payable for each day of default, up to a maximum of 50% of the tax payable, and if the calculated penalty is less than Rs 40,000 or no tax is payable it is Rs 40,000, while for a salaried person whose salary is at least 75% of total income and below Rs 5 million the minimum penalty is Rs 5,000. The Section 182A ATL surcharge is separate: if you file after the due date you may need to pay it to be included on the Active Taxpayer List (ATL), and the name is included only after payment. FBR has also introduced a rule under which an individual who files the latest tax year's return late may submit an undertaking through IRIS (Form ATL-U) and be included on the ATL without paying the surcharge, subject to the stated conditions. The exact amount depends on your income, tax payable, filing date, and whether the ATL-U conditions apply, so do not rely on old online guides and check the amount in IRIS or with FBR before paying.
answer_ur: Aap aam taur par late income tax return phir bhi file kar sakte hain, lekin late filing par do alag charges lag sakte hain. Section 182 ka late filing penalty payable tax ka har din ke default par 0.1% hai jo payable tax ke 50% se zyada nahi ho sakta, aur agar yeh raqam Rs 40,000 se kam ho ya tax payable na ho to penalty Rs 40,000 hai, jabke salary agar total income ka kam az kam 75% ho aur Rs 5 million se kam ho to minimum penalty Rs 5,000 hai. Section 182A ka ATL surcharge alag hai, deadline ke baad return file karne par Active Taxpayer List (ATL) mein shamil hone ke liye dena par sakta hai, aur naam payment ke baad hi shamil hota hai. FBR ke aik rule ke mutabiq individual jo latest tax year ka return late file kare woh IRIS mein Form ATL-U undertaking de kar shartat poori hone par surcharge ke baghair ATL mein shamil ho sakta hai. Asal raqam income, payable tax, filing date aur ATL-U ki shartat par depend karti hai, is liye purane online guides par bharosa na karein aur payment se pehle IRIS ya FBR se raqam confirm karein.

question: What is a wealth statement, and who needs one?
variants: What is a wealth statement? | Who has to file a wealth statement? | Do I need a wealth statement with my tax return? | Wealth statement kya hota hai? | Wealth statement kis ko file karna hota hai? | wealth statement kis ko deni hoti hai | wealth reconciliation | wealth reconciliation statement | reconciliation of net assets | assets liabilities statement | assets liabilities FBR | property vehicles bank balance wealth statement | foreign income assets statement | foreign assets statement | 116A | AOP wealth statement | non resident wealth statement | wealth tax Pakistan | wealth statement IRIS | Who has to submit wealth statement | Wealth statement kya hota hai | Wealth statement kis ko dena hota hai | Wealth statement kab dena parta hai | do I need to declare my assets and property | assets declare karne parte hain? | need to list house car savings in return? | wealth statment | wealth statement | wealth stmt | wealth statement kya hai | asset declaration in return | jaidad declare karna zaroori hai? | do I declare my property and bank balance | what is wealth reconciliation | wealth statement lazmi hai kya
answer_en: A wealth statement is a declaration you give FBR showing your assets, liabilities, and annual personal expenses for the tax year, filed with your income tax return on IRIS together with a wealth reconciliation statement that explains the increase or decrease in your net assets during the year. It generally includes assets such as property, vehicles, bank balances, cash, investments, and jewellery, and liabilities such as loans. Every resident individual who files an income tax return must furnish a wealth statement and wealth reconciliation statement with that return, every member of an AOP must furnish them with the AOP's return, and FBR can require an individual to file one through a written notice; a non-resident individual is generally not required to file one, although FBR can issue a notice requiring it. A resident individual with foreign income of at least USD 10,000 or foreign assets worth at least USD 100,000 must also file a separate foreign income and assets statement under Section 116A. Pakistan has no separate wealth tax, and you should give accurate asset, liability, and expense details without guessing values or leaving out assets.
answer_ur: Wealth statement aik declaration hai jo aap FBR ko dete hain aur jis mein tax year ke assets, liabilities aur saalana personal kharche hote hain, yeh IRIS par income tax return ke sath file hoti hai aur sath wealth reconciliation statement bhi hoti hai jo saal ke doran net assets mein izafa ya kami ki wajah batati hai. Is mein aam taur par property, gaariyan, bank balance, cash, investments aur zewar jaise assets, aur loans jaisi liabilities shamil hoti hain. Har resident individual jo income tax return file karta hai usay return ke sath wealth statement aur wealth reconciliation statement deni hoti hai, AOP ka har member AOP ke return ke sath deta hai, aur FBR written notice se kisi individual ko wealth statement dene ka keh sakta hai; non-resident individual ko aam taur par yeh nahi deni hoti, lekin FBR notice de kar mang sakta hai. Resident individual ki foreign income kam az kam USD 10,000 ya foreign assets kam az kam USD 100,000 hon to Section 116A ke tehat alag foreign income and assets statement bhi deni hoti hai. Pakistan mein alag wealth tax nahi hai, aur assets, liabilities aur kharchon ki sahi details dein, values andaza se na likhein aur koi asset na chhupayein.

answer_en: Yes, a student can register with FBR and file an income tax return if they have a valid CNIC, because FBR treats an individual as registered after e-enrolment on IRIS and uses the individual's 13-digit CNIC as the NTN/Registration Number. A student with no taxable income can file a nil return, which may help the student appear on the Active Taxpayer List (ATL), subject to FBR's ATL rules. A student must file if they meet FBR's filing conditions, such as taxable income above the applicable threshold, ownership of certain assets, or being required to file by notice, and these thresholds change with the law and budget. Being registered for an NTN does not automatically mean a student must file every year, but if filing is required for a tax year the return should be filed for that year. If you are unsure, check fbr.gov.pk or contact FBR, and if you do not yet have a CNIC contact FBR or visit a Tax House facilitation counter before trying to register.
answer_ur: Ji haan, student valid CNIC ke sath FBR mein register ho sakta hai aur income tax return file kar sakta hai, kyunke FBR individual ko IRIS par e-enrolment ke baad registered samajhta hai aur 13 digit CNIC hi NTN/Registration Number hota hai. Agar student ki koi taxable income nahi to woh nil return file kar sakta hai, jis se FBR ke ATL rules ke tehat student Active Taxpayer List (ATL) mein aa sakta hai. Student ko return tab file karni hoti hai jab FBR ki filing conditions poori hon, jaise taxable income applicable limit se zyada ho, certain assets ka ownership ho, ya FBR ka notice aaye, aur yeh limits qanoon aur budget ke sath badalti hain. NTN ke liye register hone ka matlab yeh nahi ke har saal return file karna zaroori hai, lekin kisi tax year ke liye filing zaroori ho to us saal ki return file karni chahiye. Confusion ho to fbr.gov.pk dekhein ya FBR se rabta karein, aur agar abhi CNIC nahi hai to registration se pehle FBR se rabta karein ya Tax House facilitation counter par jayein.

question: Is freelance income taxable in Pakistan?
variants: Do freelancers pay tax in Pakistan? | Is Upwork or Fiverr income taxable? | Freelancing ki income par tax lagta hai? | Freelancer ko kitna tax dena parta hai? | freelance income tax | freelancing tax | Upwork tax Pakistan | Fiverr tax Pakistan | foreign client tax | IT export tax | IT enabled services tax | PSEB certificate bank | 0.25% IT export | final tax freelancer | freelance income Pakistan | domestic client freelance tax | freelancer tax return | freelancer filer | Is income from freelancing taxed in Pakistan? | Does FBR tax online earnings? | Freelancing ki income par tax hai? | Kya freelancer ko tax dena parta hai | Online kamai par tax lagta hai? | tax on earnings from foreign clients in dollars | dollars client abroad income tax | dollar kamai par tax | is freelance earning taxable | freelance income taxable | freelancing taxable hai? | online earning taxable | do I pay tax on money earned from international clients | foreign clients se kamai par tax | Upwork earnings taxable? | Fiverr income tax
answer_en: Yes, freelance income is generally taxable in Pakistan, and the treatment depends mainly on whether your work is an export of IT or IT-enabled services, whether you are registered and certified by PSEB, and whether your client is in Pakistan or abroad. For foreign clients, IT or IT-enabled service exporters registered and certified by PSEB pay a reduced final tax of 0.25% of export proceeds, extended from 2026 up to Tax Year 2029, if they meet the Section 154A conditions including receiving proceeds in foreign exchange through the required banking channel, while IT exporters not registered or certified by PSEB pay a final tax of 1% of export proceeds. For other services exported to foreign clients, FBR's rate material shows a 1% fixed tax when receipts are brought into Pakistan in foreign exchange through a normal banking channel, so confirm your service in FBR's current Withholding Tax Rate Card. If your client is in Pakistan, your income is generally taxed under the normal income-tax rules, and what you owe depends on your total taxable income and the current slabs. Even if no further tax is due, register for an NTN and file your annual income tax return if required, because filer status can also affect withholding rates, and note that the 0.25% rate is not for every freelancer but only for eligible IT/IT-enabled service exporters registered and certified by PSEB.
answer_ur: Ji haan, freelancing ki income Pakistan mein aam taur par taxable hoti hai, aur treatment is baat par depend karta hai ke kaam IT/IT-enabled services ka export hai ya nahi, aap PSEB mein registered aur certified hain ya nahi, aur client Pakistan mein hai ya bahar. Bahar ke clients ke liye PSEB mein registered aur certified IT/IT-enabled services exporters export proceeds par 0.25% reduced final tax dete hain (jo 2026 se Tax Year 2029 tak extend hai) agar Section 154A ki shartein poori hon, jin mein export proceeds foreign exchange mein required banking channel se lena shamil hai, jabke PSEB mein registered/certified na hone wale IT exporters par export proceeds ka 1% final tax hai. IT ke ilawa doosri exported services ke liye FBR ke rate material mein foreign exchange mein normal banking channel se receipts aane par 1% fixed tax ka zikr hai, is liye apni service ke liye FBR ka current Withholding Tax Rate Card dekhein. Pakistan ke clients ki soorat mein income aam taur par normal income tax rules ke tehat aati hai aur tax aapki total taxable income aur current slabs par depend karta hai. Tax na bhi banta ho to bhi agar zaroori ho to NTN register karwayein aur annual income tax return file karein, kyunke filer ya non-filer hona withholding rates par bhi asar daal sakta hai, aur 0.25% rate har freelancer ke liye nahi balke sirf PSEB mein registered aur certified eligible IT/IT-enabled service exporters ke liye hai.
source_line: Based on FBR Section 154A material and PSEB (fbr.gov.pk, techdestination.com). FBR helpline: 051-111-772-772

question: What tax rate applies to freelancers?

answer_en: The rate depends on where your clients are, what service you provide, and whether you are registered and certified by PSEB. For foreign clients, IT and IT-enabled services registered and certified by PSEB pay a reduced final tax of 0.25% of export proceeds, extended from 2026 up to Tax Year 2029, while for other exported services FBR's Budget 2026-27 material says total tax collection on export proceeds was reduced from 2% to 1.25%, with the exact split depending on the provision and service, so 1% should not be treated as a universal rate for every non-IT freelancer. Export proceeds should be received in foreign exchange through the required banking channel, and your PSEB registration or certificate and bank documentation may be needed to prove eligibility for the reduced IT-export rate. For Pakistani clients, the client may deduct withholding tax before paying you, and FBR's Finance Bill 2026 states 15% for independent professional services such as doctors, lawyers, architects, accountants, software engineers, and developers working independently, or 30% where the person is not on the Active Taxpayer List, subject to the applicable conditions. This withholding is not necessarily your final yearly income tax, which depends on your total taxable income, deductions, and the slabs for the tax year, and the 0.25% rate is only for eligible PSEB-registered and certified IT exporters, so check the current FBR rate card before relying on any rate.
answer_ur: Rate is par depend karta hai ke clients kahan hain, aap konsi service dete hain, aur aap PSEB mein registered aur certified hain ya nahi. Bahar ke clients ke liye PSEB mein registered aur certified IT aur IT-enabled services par export proceeds par 0.25% reduced final tax hai jo 2026 se Tax Year 2029 tak extend hai, jabke doosri exported services ke liye FBR ke Budget 2026-27 material ke mutabiq export proceeds par total tax collection 2% se kam ho kar 1.25% hui hai, aur exact split provision aur service par depend karta hai, is liye har non-IT freelancer ke liye 1% universal rate na samjhein. Export proceeds foreign exchange mein required banking channel se aane chahiyein, aur reduced IT-export rate ke liye PSEB registration/certificate aur bank documentation zaroori ho sakti hai. Pakistani clients payment se pehle withholding tax kaat sakte hain, aur independent professional services (doctors, lawyers, architects, accountants, software engineers aur developers jo independently kaam karte hain) ke liye FBR ke Finance Bill 2026 mein 15% rate hai, jo Active Taxpayer List mein na hone par applicable shartat ke tehat 30% ho sakta hai. Yeh withholding zaroori nahi ke final yearly tax ho, kyunke final tax total taxable income, deductions aur slabs par depend karta hai, aur 0.25% rate sirf eligible PSEB-registered IT exporters ke liye hai, is liye bharosa karne se pehle FBR ka current rate card dekhein.

answer_en: Yes, Pakistan provides a reduced tax rate for eligible exporters of IT and IT-enabled services. answer_en: PSEB means the Pakistan Software Export Board, a government body that supports Pakistan's IT and IT-enabled services (ITeS) sector and IT exports, and registration means becoming a member and receiving an official PSEB membership certificate, with separate categories for freelancers, companies, and call centers. Freelancer membership may provide a reduced income-tax rate of 0.25% on export proceeds of IT and IT-enabled services subject to FBR conditions (PSEB says registered freelancers pay 0.25% while non-registered freelancers pay 1%), 50% retention on ESFCA subject to State Bank of Pakistan rules, and visa facilitation and other membership support. To apply you must be an individual working independently in IT/ITeS with a valid personal NTN with no business name and a personal bank account, and you create an account on portal.techdestination.com, upload scanned copies of your personal NTN, CNIC (both sides), and a personal bank-account opening or maintenance letter or certificate, and after initial approval pay the fee and upload the receipt for final approval. The freelancer fee is Rs 1,000 per year and renewal is Rs 2,000 per year, registration is processed in 1 working day after complete documentation (the general registration page says usually 2-5 working days after payment verification), and renewal each year requires your latest income tax return, Form 114. PSEB registration is separate from FBR/IRIS registration, and you generally need an FBR NTN before applying to PSEB.

answer_en: No, you do not need to register a company to start freelancing in Pakistan, and many freelancers work as individuals. As an individual you register with FBR through IRIS to get your personal NTN/Registration Number, file your income-tax return each year if required, and are taxed on your freelance income in your own name; you may also register with PSEB as a freelancer if you provide IT or IT-enabled services and meet its requirements, which include a personal NTN with no business name, so if you have a registered business use PSEB's company/firm category instead. You may consider a business or company if you want to hire staff or work as a team, if clients require a company invoice, contract, or business bank account, or if you want a legal structure that separates business liabilities from personal assets, which a limited company can do but a sole proprietorship generally does not. Adding a business name to your NTN does not create a separate legal entity, as a sole proprietor remains personally responsible, and FBR says an individual may add multiple businesses under FBR registration without that making any of them a separate company. Sales-tax registration depends on your services and provincial rules, and exported services may be treated differently from services supplied within Pakistan, so do not assume every freelancer must register; banks and platforms differ, and Payoneer offers individual accounts for freelancers without a registered business, so consult a qualified accountant or lawyer if you plan to hire staff, sign large contracts, or receive payments in a company name.

NTN mein business ka naam add karne se alag legal entity nahi banti aur sole proprietor zaati taur par zimmedar rehta hai, aur FBR ke mutabiq individual multiple businesses add kar sakta hai lekin is se woh alag company nahi ban jati. Sales tax registration services aur soobai rules par depend karti hai, exported services ke rules mukhtalif ho sakte hain, aur Payoneer registered business ke baghair freelancers ko individual account deta hai, is liye staff rakhne, bare contracts sign karne ya company ke naam se payments lene se pehle qualified accountant ya lawyer se mashwara karein.

answer_en: The legal way is to receive your foreign earnings through an authorized dealer bank in Pakistan so the payment is recorded as export income, for example by direct withdrawal to your Pakistani bank account from Upwork or Fiverr if they offer it (check your earnings or Get Paid settings), through Payoneer linked to your own Pakistani bank account, by a bank wire or SWIFT transfer from your client, or into an Exporters' Special Foreign Currency Account (ESFCA) if you want to keep part of your foreign earnings in foreign currency. Use a bank account in your own name matching your CNIC, give your bank a one-time declaration of the online services you provide, ask your bank to confirm the purpose code it uses (SBP's code list gives 9185 for freelance computer and information services, but the bank must apply the code that matches your declared service, so do not assume it applies to every freelancer), and ask for the PRC (Proceeds Realisation Certificate) or e-PRC as proof that the funds were realized in Pakistan. Keep invoices, client contracts, and platform earning statements, and declare the income in your yearly income tax return. If you use an ESFCA, SBP says eligible freelancers may retain the higher of US$5,000 per month or 50% of export proceeds, and banks must process inward export receipts within one working day, subject to the applicable rules. Apne CNIC se match karte hue apne naam ka bank account istemal karein, bank ko apni online services ki one-time declaration dein, bank se confirm karein ke kaun sa purpose code use ho raha hai (SBP ke code list mein freelance computer aur information services ke liye 9185 hai, magar bank aapki declared service ke mutabiq code lagata hai), aur PRC (Proceeds Realisation Certificate) ya e-PRC lein jo is baat ka saboot hai ke funds bahar se aaye aur Pakistan mein realize hue. Invoices, client contracts aur platform earning statements sambhal kar rakhein aur income apni saalana income tax return mein declare karein. ESFCA mein SBP ke mutabiq eligible freelancers mahana US$5,000 ya export proceeds ka 50%, jo zyada ho, retain kar sakte hain, aur banks ko inward export receipts ek working day mein process karni hoti hain, applicable rules ke tehat. answer_en: A home remittance is money sent to Pakistan by a Pakistani living abroad, usually to support family members, and SBP describes it as an important source of foreign exchange that supports families and Pakistan's balance of payments. Your Upwork, Fiverr, or other foreign-client payment is not a home remittance because it is payment for services you provided to a client abroad, so it is generally treated as an export of services, and SBP's code list classifies remittances received by resident individuals or households from reputed overseas IT firms and online platforms for freelance computer and information services under purpose code 9185. Ask your bank to record eligible freelance IT/ITeS export payments under the correct applicable code, tell it the payment is for freelance IT/ITeS services provided to a foreign client, request proof of inward remittance such as a PRC, and do not describe client payments as home remittances in your tax return, since they are business or export income. If a relative abroad sends you money for family support, that can be a genuine home remittance, and you should keep it separate from your freelance income and records. Keep invoices, contracts, platform payment records, bank receipts, and your income-tax return consistent.
answer_ur: Home remittance woh paise hote hain jo bahar rehne wale Pakistani aam taur par ghar walon ki madad ke liye Pakistan bhejte hain, aur SBP ke mutabiq yeh foreign exchange ka ahem zariya hai jo families aur balance of payments ki madad karta hai. Upwork, Fiverr ya kisi doosre foreign client ki payment home remittance nahi hai kyunke yeh bahar ke client ko di gayi services ki payment hai, is liye aam taur par services ki export gini jati hai, aur SBP ke code list mein resident individuals/households ko reputed overseas IT firms aur online platforms se freelance computer aur information services ki payment ke liye purpose code 9185 diya gaya hai. Bank se kahein ke eligible freelance IT/ITeS export payments ko correct applicable code ke tehat record kare, usay batayein ke payment foreign client ko di gayi freelance IT/ITeS services ki hai, inward remittance ka proof jaise PRC maangein, aur tax return mein client payments ko home remittance na likhein kyunke yeh business ya export income hai. Agar bahar rehne wala rishtedar ghar ke kharche ke liye paise bheje to woh asal home remittance ho sakti hai, usay apni freelance income aur records se alag rakhein. Invoices, contracts, platform payment records, bank receipts aur income tax return aik doosre se match hon.
source_line: Based on SBP Invisible and Capital Receipts Code List No. 5 (sbp.org.pk).

question: Is Payoneer allowed in Pakistan?

answer_en: Yes, Payoneer is available in Pakistan and is commonly used by freelancers to receive payments from overseas clients and platforms such as Fiverr and Upwork, and you can withdraw the money to a linked Pakistani bank account in Pakistani rupees; Payoneer also offers an individual account for freelancers without a registered business. Open the account in your own name, link a Pakistani bank account in your own name (or in your registered business name if applicable), and note that Payoneer says the withdrawal account may need to match your Payoneer account details. Keep records of Payoneer statements, invoices, client details, and platform earnings, and when the money reaches your bank ask which SBP purpose code it applied, as SBP lists 9185 for eligible freelance computer and information services. Declare your freelance income in your income-tax return, because receiving money through Payoneer does not make it tax-free. Check the exchange rate, conversion amount, fees, and withdrawal time in your Payoneer account before withdrawing, since Payoneer says withdrawals generally reach the linked account within two business days but timing and charges can vary, and use Payoneer only for your own legitimate freelance or business payments.
answer_ur: Ji haan, Payoneer Pakistan mein available hai aur freelancers isay overseas clients aur Fiverr, Upwork jaise platforms se payments lene ke liye aam taur par use karte hain, aur aap paise linked Pakistani bank account mein Pakistani rupees mein withdraw kar sakte hain; Payoneer bina registered business wale freelancers ko individual account bhi deta hai. Account apne naam par kholein, apne naam ka Pakistani bank account link karein (ya applicable ho to registered business ke naam ka), aur dhyan rakhein ke Payoneer ke mutabiq withdrawal account ki details Payoneer account se match honi chahiye. Payoneer statements, invoices, client details aur platform earnings ke records rakhein, aur jab paise bank mein aayein to bank se poochein ke kaunsa SBP purpose code lagaya, jabke SBP ne eligible freelance computer aur information services ke liye 9185 diya hai. Apni freelance income income tax return mein declare karein kyunke Payoneer se paise lene se woh tax-free nahi hoti. Withdraw karne se pehle exchange rate, conversion amount, fees aur withdrawal time check karein kyunke Payoneer ke mutabiq funds aam taur par do business days mein pohanchte hain lekin time aur charges badal sakte hain, aur Payoneer sirf apni legitimate freelance ya business payments ke liye use karein.

answer_en: SBP has not stated a fixed yearly limit on the foreign income a freelancer can receive, provided the payments are for genuine work, come through proper banking channels, and are supported by records such as invoices, contracts, and platform payment details. Since April 2026 SBP has raised the Form R threshold to above US$25,000 or equivalent in another currency, so for a single payment above US$25,000 your bank may require Form R or additional reporting details, and SBP's Form R format refers to receipts above that amount for purposes other than export of goods and family maintenance. The US$25,000 threshold relates to a single receipt, not a confirmed annual income limit, and banks may still ask questions or request documents such as your CNIC and NTN, invoices, contracts, platform records, and a description of the services for smaller payments. Receiving a large amount does not change your tax obligations, and you must still declare your taxable income in your income-tax return. This answer covers money coming into Pakistan only, as sending money abroad has separate rules, so keep your records and ask your bank about Form R for any payment above US$25,000.
answer_ur: SBP ne freelancer ke liye foreign income receive karne ki koi fixed saalana limit nahi batayi, bas payments asli kaam ki hon, proper banking channels se aayein aur invoices, contracts aur platform payment details jaise saboot maujood hon. April 2026 se SBP ne Form R ki threshold US$25,000 se zyada (ya doosri currency mein barabar raqam) kar di hai, is liye aik hi payment US$25,000 se zyada ho to bank Form R ya additional reporting details maang sakta hai, aur SBP ka Form R format export of goods aur family maintenance ke ilawa is raqam se zyada receipts ka zikr karta hai. US$25,000 threshold aik single receipt ke liye hai, confirmed saalana income limit nahi, aur bank chhoti payments par bhi CNIC, NTN, invoices, contracts, platform records aur services ki tafseel jaise documents maang sakta hai. Zyada raqam aane se tax obligations khatam nahi hoti aur taxable income income tax return mein declare karni hogi. Yeh jawab Pakistan mein aane wale paison ke bare mein hai, bahar bhejne ke alag rules hain, is liye records rakhein aur US$25,000 se zyada payment par bank se Form R poochhein.
source_line: Based on SBP press release of 6 April 2026 and Form R format (archive.sbp.org.pk).

question: What is a foreign currency account, and can I open one?
variants: What is a foreign currency account? | Can freelancers have a dollar account in Pakistan? | Foreign currency account kya hota hai? | foreign currency account pakistan | freelancer dollar account | freelancer foreign currency account | esfca retention | esfca 5000 | esfca 50 percent | esfca one working day | esfca software subscription | esfca bank account | can freelancer open dollar account | freelancer dollar account khol sakta hai | Can I open a foreign currency account? | What is an FCY account? | Foreign currency account kya hota hai | Dollar account kholna possible hai? | Can I keep dollars in my account | Can freelancers hold USD without converting | FCY account | fcy account kya hai | dollar account | foreign currency account | usd account open | dollar account Pakistan kholna | can I keep earnings in USD | USD mein paise rakh sakte hain? | exchange rate conversion zaroori hai ya dollar rakh sakte | what is a currency account in Pakistan banks | ESFCA account
answer_en: A foreign currency account holds money in a foreign currency such as US dollars instead of Pakistani rupees, and for eligible freelancers and IT companies SBP provides a special account called an Exporters' Special Foreign Currency Account (ESFCA). Yes, you can open one, because SBP instructs banks to open an ESFCA for eligible IT companies and freelancers at the same time as their primary Pakistani rupee account, so ask your bank specifically for an ESFCA. Eligible IT/ITeS export receipts can be credited to it, freelancers may retain the higher of US$5,000 per month or 50% of export proceeds, and funds can be used for eligible payments abroad such as software, online tools, subscriptions, and digital services without prior SBP approval, subject to account rules. SBP's April 2026 circular requires banks to process inward export receipts and outward remittances from ESFCAs within one working day, and you give your bank a one-time description of your services instead of paperwork for every payment. Banks may have different account-opening processes, and keeping money in an ESFCA does not remove your tax obligations, so you must still declare your taxable income and keep invoices, contracts, and bank receipts.
answer_ur: Foreign currency account aisa bank account hota hai jis mein paise Pakistani rupees ke bajaye US dollars jaisi foreign currency mein rakhe jate hain, aur eligible freelancers aur IT companies ke liye SBP ka khaas account Exporters' Special Foreign Currency Account (ESFCA) hai. Ji haan, aap khol sakte hain kyunke SBP banks ko hukm deta hai ke eligible IT companies aur freelancers ka ESFCA unke primary Pakistani rupee account ke saath hi kholein, is liye bank se specifically ESFCA maangein. Eligible IT/ITeS export receipts is mein credit ho sakti hain, freelancers US$5,000 per month ya export proceeds ka 50%, jo zyada ho, rakh sakte hain, aur funds ko software, online tools, subscriptions aur digital services jaisi eligible foreign payments ke liye SBP ki pehle ijazat ke baghair account rules ke tehat use kar sakte hain. SBP ki April 2026 circular ke mutabiq banks ko ESFCA mein aane wali export receipts aur is se jane wali remittances aik working day mein process karni hoti hain, aur aap bank ko apni services ki aik dafa tafseel dete hain, har payment ke liye alag kaghazat nahi. Har bank ka process mukhtalif ho sakta hai, aur ESFCA mein dollars rakhne se tax obligations khatam nahi hoti, is liye taxable income declare karein aur invoices, contracts aur bank receipts rakhein.
source_line: Based on SBP EPD Circular Letter No. 06 of 2026 and Foreign Exchange Manual (sbp.org.pk).

question: How do banks treat freelance income (proof of income)?
variants: How do banks treat freelance income? | What is proof of income for a freelancer? | Bank freelancer ki income ko kaise dekhta hai? | Freelancer income ka saboot kya hota hai? | proof of income freelancer | freelance income bank | bank freelancer income documents | prc meaning | s-prc | proceeds realization certificate | prc for freelance income | prc tax return | prc bank pakistan | bank asks freelance payment documents | freelancer invoice contract bank | freelancer income ka saboot | e-prc kaise lein | How do banks see freelance income as proof? | What proof of income can freelancer show to bank | Bank freelance income ka proof kaise maanta hai | Freelancer ke liye income proof kya hai | Bank salary slip maangta hai, freelancer kya dikhaye | bank loan freelancer income proof | income proof | income proof freelancer | income proof bank freelancer | proof of income bank | bank mein income proof kya dein | what documents prove freelance earnings to a bank | freelancer ke liye bank income certificate | how can a freelancer show income for card or loan
answer_en: When a foreign freelance payment reaches your Pakistani bank account, the bank may ask where it came from and what services you provided, because banks follow customer due-diligence and foreign-exchange requirements. PSEB's guidance says banks may commonly ask for your CNIC and NTN, a contract or agreement with the client, a screenshot or record from the platform such as Upwork or Fiverr, and an invoice or email evidence of the work and payment. A key document is the Proceeds Realization Certificate (PRC), which SBP describes as documentary proof that funds received from abroad were realized in Pakistan; the bank can issue an electronic PRC (e-PRC) for an individual inward remittance, or a Statement of PRCs (S-PRC) covering multiple payments. Keep the PRC with your invoice, contract, platform earnings record, and bank statement, and note that a PRC supports the source and nature of your income but does not decide your tax rate or remove your tax obligations. To make your income easy to prove, receive payments in an account in your own name (or registered business name if applicable), save all records, file your income-tax return when required, and ask your bank which documents it accepts if you apply for a loan or credit card, since policies differ by bank.
answer_ur: Jab foreign freelance payment aapke Pakistani bank account mein aati hai to bank poochh sakta hai ke payment kahan se aayi aur aap ne kaunsi services di thin, kyunke banks customer due-diligence aur foreign exchange requirements follow karte hain. PSEB ki guidance ke mutabiq banks aam taur par CNIC aur NTN, client ke sath contract ya agreement, Upwork ya Fiverr jaise platform ka screenshot ya record, aur invoice ya email ka saboot maang sakte hain. Aham document Proceeds Realization Certificate (PRC) hai jisay SBP aisi documentary proof kehta hai ke bahar se aaye funds Pakistan mein realize hue; bank aik inward remittance ke liye electronic PRC (e-PRC) ya kai payments ke liye Statement of PRCs (S-PRC) issue kar sakta hai. PRC ko invoice, contract, platform earnings record aur bank statement ke sath rakhein, aur yaad rakhein ke PRC income ka source aur nature prove karta hai magar tax rate decide nahi karta aur tax obligations khatam nahi karta. Income ka saboot aasan banane ke liye apne naam ke bank account mein (ya applicable ho to registered business ke naam ke account mein) payments lein, tamam records save karein, zaroorat ho to income tax return file karein, aur loan ya credit card ke liye bank se poochein ke woh kaunse documents qabool karta hai kyunke har bank ke rules alag hote hain.
source_line: Based on SBP e-PRC/S-PRC circulars (sbp.org.pk) and PSEB Freelancer Registration page (techdestination.com).

question: Is tax deducted when I receive foreign payments in my bank account?
variants: Is tax deducted when I withdraw foreign payments? | Is tax deducted on Upwork or Fiverr withdrawals? | Does the bank cut tax on foreign payments? | Foreign payments par tax kat’ta hai? | Payoneer se paise nikalwane par tax lagta hai? | tax deducted on foreign payment | bank tax deduction | withholding tax | Upwork tax | Fiverr tax | Payoneer tax | foreign payment tax | 0.25 percent tax | 1 percent tax | final tax | final tax conditions | freelancer final tax | foreign payment par tax | bank tax kaat leta hai | Payoneer se paise nikalwane par tax | cash withdrawal tax | non filer cash withdrawal tax | What is Section 154A? | Who can get the 0.25% tax rate? | Does PSEB registration guarantee the 0.25% rate? | When does the 154A tax become final tax? | What happens if I do not file my tax return? | Can I opt out of final taxation under Section 154A? | Does the Active Taxpayer List affect the 0.25% or 1% rate? | Kya PSEB registration se 0.25% tax rate milta hai? | 154A tax final kab hota hai? | Agar main tax return file nahi karta to kya hoga? | Is tax cut when foreign payment comes in? | Does the bank deduct tax on remittance | Foreign payment aane par tax katta hai? | Remittance par tax deduct hota hai? | Why was money deducted from my incoming payment | Bank ne tax kaat liya remittance par | tax on remittance | remittance tax | tax deduction foreign payment | tax kata hai remittance | bank tax cut incoming payment | deduction on foreign receipts | payment aate hi paise kat gaye | withholding on foreign remittance bank | is there withholding on foreign payments | Will bank deduct tax on international payment | international payment par bank tax kaat lega
answer_en: Yes, when your foreign payment is realized through your Pakistani bank, the bank deducts tax under Section 154A of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 as withholding tax at source, so you do not pay it separately later. The rate is 0.25% of export proceeds if you export qualifying computer software, IT services, or IT-enabled services and are registered with and certified by PSEB (a concessionary rate extended through Tax Year 2029), and 1% of export proceeds for any other export of services under Section 154A, and this applies whether the money comes by direct bank transfer, an Upwork withdrawal to your local bank, or Payoneer sent to your bank account. The deduction is final tax on that export income only if you meet the Section 154A conditions, which include filing your income tax return, filing any required withholding statements, and not claiming foreign-tax credit for that income; otherwise the income may be taxed under the normal income-tax rules. Ask your bank for the tax deduction certificate or receipt along with your PRC, declare the export income and tax deducted in your return, check that the correct rate was applied, and if you are PSEB-registered but the bank deducts 1% show your PSEB registration or certificate and ask it to correct the treatment. Separately, if you are not on the Active Taxpayer List a different advance tax may apply when you withdraw cash above the applicable daily limit, and for the latest rules please check fbr.gov.pk or call the FBR helpline 051 111 772 772.
answer_ur: Ji haan, jab aapki foreign payment Pakistani bank ke zariye realize hoti hai to bank Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 ki Section 154A ke tehat withholding tax kaat leta hai, aur aapko yeh baad mein alag se ada nahi karna parta. Agar aap qualifying computer software, IT services ya IT-enabled services export karte hain aur PSEB mein registered aur certified hain to export proceeds ka 0.25% kat'ta hai (yeh concessionary rate Tax Year 2029 tak extend hai), aur Section 154A ke tehat kisi aur service export par 1%, aur yeh seedha bank transfer, Upwork ka local bank withdrawal ya Payoneer se bank account mein aane wali payment par bhi lagu hota hai. Yeh katauti us export income par final tax tab hi hai jab Section 154A ki shartein poori hon, yani income tax return file karna, zaroori withholding statements file karna aur us income par foreign tax credit claim na karna, warna income normal income-tax rules ke tehat tax ho sakti hai. Bank se PRC ke sath tax deduction certificate ya receipt maangein, export income aur kati hui tax return mein declare karein, dekhein ke sahi rate laga ya nahi, aur PSEB-registered hone ke bawajood bank 1% kaate to PSEB certificate dikha kar treatment theek karwayein. Alag baat yeh ke Active Taxpayer List mein na hone par daily limit se zyada cash nikalwane par alag advance tax lag sakta hai, aur taaza rules ke liye fbr.gov.pk dekhein ya FBR helpline 051 111 772 772 par call karein.
source_line: Based on FBR Section 154A guidance and FBR withholding-tax rate card (fbr.gov.pk). FBR helpline: 051 111 772 772

question: What if I miss the filing deadline?
variants: What happens if I miss the tax return deadline? | Can I file my return after the last date? | What is the penalty for late filing? | Return ki last date miss ho jaye to kya hoga? | Late return file kar sakte hain? | missed tax deadline | Section 182 | 182 penalty | ATL removed | removed from ATL | filer status lost | Rs 25000 surcharge | ATL-U | Form ATL-U | ATL-U IRIS | ATL undertaking | property undertaking | six months property | rejoin ATL | return ki last date miss | late return file | ATL se naam nikal gaya | ATL mein wapas kaise aayein | What is the late-filing penalty under Section 182? | How do I get back on the Active Taxpayer List after a late return? | What is Form ATL-U and who can use it? | Does Form ATL-U stop me from buying property? | How long does the ATL-U property undertaking last? | What happens if I buy property after submitting ATL-U? | Can I get an extension for filing my tax return? | Late return ka jurmana kitna hai? | ATL se nikal gaya hoon wapas kaise aaun? | Form ATL-U kya hai aur kaun use kar sakta hai? | What if I did not file my return on time? | Deadline guzar gayi return file nahi kiya | I missed the due date, what now | Return ki date nikal gayi ab kya karun | Filing deadline pass ho gayi hai to kya kare | I forgot to submit return, can I still file | missed deadline | deadline miss | deadline guzar gayi | date nikal gayi | too late to file return? | kya late return file kar sakta hoon | what to do after due date has passed | return nahi bhara aur date nikal gayi | filing time over what to do | Agar deadline miss ho jaye to ab kya karna chahiye | what to do if the deadline is missed
answer_en: You can still file, since IRIS accepts late income tax returns and filing late is much better than not filing, but there can be consequences. Under Section 182 FBR can charge a penalty of 0.1% of the tax payable for each day of default up to a maximum of 50% of the tax payable, with a minimum of generally Rs 40,000 if the calculated penalty is lower or no tax is payable, or Rs 5,000 for a person with at least 75% salary income and salary below Rs 5 million. If you file after the due date you may be removed from the Active Taxpayer List (ATL) and treated as a non-filer for higher withholding taxes on banking and property transactions until restored, and an individual can return by paying the ATL surcharge (reported as Rs 25,000 under current rules) or by filing the latest tax year return late through IRIS and submitting Form ATL-U, which lets an eligible individual rejoin without the surcharge subject to a six-month undertaking, from the IRIS acknowledgement date, not to purchase, acquire, or obtain ownership or beneficial interest in any property. FBR can verify compliance and, if it finds a breach, withdraw the benefit and remove you from the ATL under the normal late-filer rules. If you may miss the deadline, contact your tax office before it and ask whether you qualify for an extension on reasonable grounds, since a return filed within an approved extension is treated as on time and FBR will not automatically extend for everyone; for the latest rules check fbr.gov.pk or call the FBR helpline 051 111 772 772.
answer_ur: Aap phir bhi file kar sakte hain kyunke IRIS late income tax return qabool karta hai aur bilkul file na karne se late file karna behtar hai, lekin consequences ho sakte hain. Section 182 ke tehat FBR payable tax ka har din 0.1% jurmana laga sakta hai jo payable tax ke 50% se zyada nahi ho sakta, aur calculated jurmana Rs 40,000 se kam ho ya tax payable na ho to aam taur par minimum Rs 40,000 hai, jabke income ka kam az kam 75% salary ho aur salary Rs 5 million se kam ho to minimum Rs 5,000 hai. Due date ke baad file karne par aap Active Taxpayer List (ATL) se nikal sakte hain aur wapas aane tak banking aur property transactions par non-filer samjhe ja kar zyada withholding tax de sakte hain, aur individual ATL surcharge (current rules mein Rs 25,000 report kiya gaya) de kar ya latest tax year ki late return IRIS par file kar ke Form ATL-U submit kar ke wapas aa sakta hai, jo surcharge ke baghair hota hai lekin IRIS acknowledgement ki date se chhe mahine tak kisi bhi property ki ownership ya beneficial interest khareedne ya hasil karne se qataar nahi karne ki undertaking deni hoti hai. FBR compliance check kar sakta hai aur breach milne par yeh benefit withdraw kar ke aap ko normal late-filer rules ke tehat ATL se nikal sakta hai. Agar deadline miss hone wali ho to deadline se pehle tax office se rabta kar ke reasonable grounds par extension maangein kyunke manzoor shuda extension ke andar file kiya gaya return waqt par gina jata hai aur FBR sab ke liye khud ba khud extension nahi deta, aur taaza rules ke liye fbr.gov.pk dekhein ya 051 111 772 772 par call karein.

question: How do I correct or revise a filed return?
