answer_en: Yes, if you find an omission or wrong statement in a filed return you can file a revised return under Section 114(6) of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, which replaces the original return for tax purposes and is treated as an amended assessment. Within 60 days of filing the original return you can file the revised return yourself through IRIS without the Commissioner's approval, even if the correction reduces your tax, but you must include signed written reasons, attach revised accounts or audited accounts if your return required accounts (the Commissioner may waive this), and pay any additional tax, default surcharge, and applicable amount under Section 114(6A) if the correction increases your tax. After 60 days, in the circumstances where approval is required, apply to your Commissioner through IRIS with reasons, and if no written approval order is issued within 60 days of your request, approval is treated as granted, after which you file the revised return with the required reasons and documents. Keep supporting documents such as invoices, bank statements, or platform records, and if the mistake was made by FBR you may need a separate rectification application under Section 221 instead, which is not the normal way to correct your own omission. If IRIS will not let you revise, call the FBR helpline 051 111 772 772 or contact your tax office, and for the latest rules check fbr.gov.pk.
answer_ur: Ji haan, agar filed return mein koi cheez reh gayi ho ya ghalat maloomat ho to aap Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 ki Section 114(6) ke tehat revised return file kar sakte hain, jo tax ke maqasid ke liye asal return ki jagah leta hai aur amended assessment samjha jata hai. Asal return ke 60 din ke andar aap IRIS par khud revised return file kar sakte hain aur tax kam hone par bhi Commissioner ki manzoori zaroori nahi, lekin dastkhat shuda likhi hui wajuhaat dena, return ke sath accounts zaroori hon to revised accounts ya audited accounts attach karna (Commissioner maaf kar sakta hai), aur correction se tax barhe to extra tax, default surcharge aur Section 114(6A) ke tehat applicable raqam ada karna zaroori hai. 60 din ke baad, jin sooraton mein manzoori zaroori ho, IRIS ke zariye Commissioner se wajuhaat ke sath ijazat maangein, aur agar request ke 60 din ke andar likhi hui approval order issue na ho to manzoori de di gayi samjhi jati hai, phir revised return zaroori wajuhaat aur documents ke sath file karein. Invoices, bank statements ya platform records jaise supporting documents rakhein, aur agar ghalti FBR ki taraf se ho to Section 221 ke tehat alag rectification application ki zaroorat ho sakti hai jo apni ghalti theek karne ka aam tareeqa nahi. Agar IRIS revision allow na kare to FBR helpline 051 111 772 772 par call karein ya tax office se rabta karein, aur taaza rules ke liye fbr.gov.pk dekhein.
source_line: Based on FBR Income Tax Ordinance Section 114(6)/(6A) and IRIS FAQ (fbr.gov.pk, e.fbr.gov.pk). FBR helpline: 051 111 772 772

question: What if I get a notice from FBR?

answer_en: Do not panic and do not ignore an FBR notice, because it does not always mean you did something wrong and may be a reminder to file, a request for information, or a check of your records. First check it is genuine by looking in your IRIS notices inbox, using FBR's Notices/Orders Verification service on IRIS, or calling the FBR helpline 051 111 772 772, and never share your IRIS password, OTP, bank details, or payment with anyone who contacts you by phone, SMS, WhatsApp, or email. Read the section cited, the tax year, what FBR is asking for, and the deadline in the notice (Section 114 is about failure to file a return, Section 176 asks for information or evidence, Section 177 is an audit notice, and Section 122 is for amendment of an assessment, for which FBR must give you an opportunity to be heard), then gather bank statements, invoices, PRCs, platform records, contracts, and previous returns, reply through IRIS with attachments before the deadline, request an extension before the deadline if you need more time, and keep copies of everything. Ignoring a notice can lead to penalties and adverse action, FBR may proceed on the information it has and make an assessment without your input, and serious cases may lead to recovery or enforcement steps; if you need help consider a registered tax adviser or lawyer, and if you disagree with an order you may appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals) within 30 days of receiving the notice of demand or complain to the Federal Tax Ombudsman if you believe FBR mishandled your case.
answer_ur: Ghabrayein nahi aur FBR ke notice ko nazar-andaz na karein kyunke notice ka matlab hamesha yeh nahi ke aap ne kuch ghalat kiya hai, yeh return file karne ki yaad dehani, maloomat ki darkhwast ya record ki jaanch ho sakti hai. Pehle apne IRIS notices inbox mein, IRIS ki Notices/Orders Verification service se ya FBR helpline 051 111 772 772 par call kar ke check karein ke notice asli hai, aur jo shakhs phone, SMS, WhatsApp ya email par rabta kare usay IRIS password, OTP, bank details ya paise kabhi na dein. Notice mein likhi section, tax year, FBR ki maang aur deadline dhyan se parhein (Section 114 return file na karne, Section 176 maloomat ya evidence dene, Section 177 audit, aur Section 122 assessment amend karne ka notice hai jis se pehle FBR ko sunne ka mauqa dena hota hai), bank statements, invoices, PRCs, platform records, contracts aur pichle returns tayyar karein, deadline se pehle IRIS par attachments ke sath jawab dein, mazeed waqt chahiye to deadline se pehle extension maangein, aur sab ki copies rakhein. Notice ignore karne par jurmana aur adverse action ho sakta hai, FBR apne paas maujood maloomat par aap ke baghair assessment kar sakta hai, aur sanjeeda soorat mein recovery ya enforcement ke qadam ho sakte hain; zaroorat ho to registered tax adviser ya wakeel se mashwara karein, aur kisi order se mutafiq na hon to notice of demand milne ke 30 din ke andar Commissioner (Appeals) ke paas appeal kar sakte hain ya agar lagta hai FBR ne case ghalat handle kiya to Federal Tax Ombudsman ko shikayat kar sakte hain.
source_line: Based on FBR IRIS Notices/Orders Verification, Income Tax Ordinance Sections 122/176/177, and Income Tax Appeals page (fbr.gov.pk). FBR helpline: 051 111 772 772

answer_en: For FBR help with taxes, NTN, IRIS, and returns, call 051 111 772 772 (from outside Pakistan +92 51 111 772 772), Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 11:30 PM, or email helpline@fbr.gov.pk, and the women's helpline is 051 9107025, Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, though timings may vary. question: How do I check whether someone is on the Active Taxpayer List?
variants: How do I check ATL status? | How to check if someone is a filer? | How to check a supplier’s or client’s ATL status? | ATL status kaise check karein? | Kisi ka filer status kaise pata karein? | check ATL status | ATL status check | active taxpayer status | check filer status | filer status check | ATL 9966 | ATL CNIC | ATL NTN | AJKATL | AJK taxpayer status | ATL online check | ATL portal | ATL download | supplier ATL status | client ATL status | vendor ATL status | filer status kaise pata karein | Active Taxpayer List mein naam kaise dekhein | ATL status badal sakta hai | ATL update | How do I check my own ATL status? | Can I check a supplier’s ATL status? | What is the difference between income tax ATL and sales tax ATL? | What does ‘Active’ mean on the ATL? | Why is someone not on the ATL? | How often is the ATL updated? | Apni ATL status kaise check karein? | Supplier ka ATL status kaise check karein? | Income tax ATL aur sales tax ATL mein kya farq hai? | ATL par active hone ka matlab kya hai? | How do I check if a person is a filer? | Verify client is on the Active Taxpayer List | Kisi ka ATL status check karna hai | Client filer hai ya nahi kaise pata karein | How to find out whether someone is a filer | ATL check | ATL check kaise | atl status | filer check | filer hai ya nahi | check filer | verify taxpayer status of client | check someone on ATL list | ATL list mein naam dekhna hai | how to see if CNIC is active taxpayer
answer_en: You can check Active Taxpayer List (ATL) status, the income tax list most people mean when asking whether someone is a filer, using a CNIC, NTN, passport number, or registration/incorporation number. By SMS, send ATL, a space, and the 13-digit CNIC without dashes to 9966 for an individual, or ATL, a space, and the 7-digit NTN to 9966 for a company or AOP; for Azad Jammu and Kashmir use AJKATL, a space, and the CNIC for an individual, or AJKATL, a space, and the 11-digit NTN for a company or AOP, also sent to 9966. Online, open FBR's Active Taxpayer List (Income Tax) page or choose it in IRIS, enter the CNIC, NTN, passport number, or registration/incorporation number, complete the verification step, and select Verify, or download the full ATL from FBR's website, which shows its latest update date, and FBR's Tax Asaan app also has verification services so check its current ATL option. ATL status can change, for example after a late return or a change in registration, so check again close to the date you need the result, especially before a payment or contract. Check someone's status only for a valid reason such as assessing a supplier or client, and do not publicly share another person's CNIC or personal details.
answer_ur: Aap kisi individual, company ya AOP ka Active Taxpayer List (ATL) status, jo income tax ki woh list hai jise log filer status ke liye poochte hain, CNIC, NTN, passport number ya registration/incorporation number se check kar sakte hain. SMS se individual ke liye ATL, space, aur 13 digit CNIC bina dashes ke likh kar 9966 par bhejein, company ya AOP ke liye ATL, space, aur 7 digit NTN likh kar 9966 par bhejein, aur Azad Jammu aur Kashmir ke individual ke liye AJKATL, space, aur CNIC, ya company/AOP ke liye AJKATL, space, aur 11 digit NTN likh kar 9966 par bhejein. Online FBR ki Active Taxpayer List (Income Tax) page kholein ya IRIS mein usay chunein, CNIC, NTN, passport number ya registration/incorporation number daal kar verification complete karein aur Verify dabayein, ya FBR ki website se poori ATL download karein jis par latest update date hoti hai, aur FBR ka Tax Asaan app bhi verification services deta hai jis ka current ATL option dekh lein. ATL status badal sakta hai, maslan late return ya registration mein tabdeeli ke baad, is liye kisi payment ya contract se pehle jis din nateeja chahiye us ke qareeb dobara check karein. Kisi ka status sirf wajah ke saath check karein, maslan supplier ya client ka, aur kisi doosre ka CNIC ya personal details publicly share na karein.
source_line: Based on FBR Active Taxpayer List page and IRIS online verification portal (fbr.gov.pk, iris.fbr.gov.pk). FBR helpline: 051 111 772 772

answer_en: Your proof of filing is the submitted return and its acknowledgement details in IRIS, and you can download or print the submitted return as a PDF. Log in at iris.fbr.gov.pk, open Declaration, find your submitted or completed return for the correct tax year, check that its status is submitted with a submission date and that it is no longer in Draft (a saved but unsubmitted task stays in Draft and moves to Completed Tasks once submitted), then use the Print option to create a PDF copy and save it safely. If IRIS shows a separate acknowledgement slip or acknowledgement number, save that too, and do the same for your wealth statement if you filed one, noting that FBR says a submitted return can no longer be edited. Download the PDF soon after submitting, keep copies in at least two places, note your NTN, tax year, submission date, and acknowledgement number if shown, and after processing check whether your name appears on the Active Taxpayer List, as your acknowledgement can serve as proof of filing in the meantime. If IRIS will not show your filed return, call the FBR helpline 051 111 772 772.
answer_ur: Aapki filing ka saboot IRIS mein submitted return aur uske acknowledgement details hain, aur aap submitted return ko PDF mein download ya print kar sakte hain. iris.fbr.gov.pk par login karein, Declaration kholein, sahi tax year ka submitted ya completed return dhoondein, dekhein ke status submitted hai, submission ki tareekh nazar aa rahi hai aur woh Draft mein nahi hai (save kiya hua magar submit na kiya hua task Draft mein rehta hai aur submit hone par Completed Tasks mein chala jata hai), phir Print ka option istemal kar ke PDF copy banayein aur mehfooz rakhein. Agar IRIS alag acknowledgement slip ya acknowledgement number dikhaye to woh bhi save karein, aur wealth statement file ki ho to uski bhi copy lein, aur yaad rakhein ke FBR ke mutabiq submit hone ke baad return mein tabdeeli nahi ho sakti. Submit karte hi PDF download kar lein, kam az kam do jagah copy rakhein, NTN, tax year, submission date aur agar nazar aaye acknowledgement number note karein, aur processing ke baad Active Taxpayer List mein naam check karein kyunke is se pehle acknowledgement filing ka saboot ho sakti hai. Agar IRIS aapka filed return nahi dikha raha to FBR helpline 051 111 772 772 par call karein.

question: What records should a freelancer keep?
variants: What records should I keep as a freelancer? | What documents do I need for my tax return? | How long should I keep my tax records? | Freelancer ko kaun sa record rakhna chahiye? | Tax ke documents kitne saal sambhal kar rakhne chahiye? | freelancer records | tax records | record keeping | documents for tax return | freelancer documents | income proof | invoices | contracts | platform statements | Upwork records | Fiverr records | bank statements | Payoneer records | Wise records | tax deduction certificate | withholding tax receipt | expense receipts | business expenses | software receipts | filed return | FBR reply | FBR correspondence | record keeping six years | tax records kitne saal | freelancer record rakhna | tax documents sambhalna | What documents should I keep for freelance income? | Do I need to keep PRCs and bank statements? | Should I keep receipts for my business expenses? | What records should I keep for an FBR audit? | Do I need a separate bank account for freelance income? | Tax records kitne saal rakhne chahiye? | Freelance income ke liye kaun se documents rakhne chahiye? | PRC aur bank statements rakhne zaroori hain? | FBR audit ke liye kaun se records chahiye? | What records should freelancers keep for tax? | Which documents should I save for tax purposes | Freelancer ko kya records rakhne chahiye | Tax ke liye kaun se records sambhalein | How long to keep tax records | records keep | records to maintain | record rakhna | kya kya save rakhun tax ke liye | freelance invoices bank statements keep | bookkeeping for freelancers Pakistan | what paperwork to retain for FBR | accounts record kitne saal rakhne chahiye | documents to maintain for audit
answer_en: Keep your tax records for six years after the end of the tax year to which they relate, and since Pakistan's income-tax year ends on 30 June, records for Tax Year 2026 (1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026) should be kept until 30 June 2032. If FBR has started any proceeding, audit, appeal, or case involving you, keep the relevant records until that proceeding is finally decided, even if six years have passed. Keep proof of income (invoices, client contracts, platform earning statements, and Upwork or Fiverr records), monthly bank statements for every account receiving freelance income with receipts and transfer records, foreign-payment records (PRCs or e-PRCs, Payoneer or Wise reports, and the currency, date, sender, and amount), and bank tax-deduction certificates or receipts, especially for tax withheld under Section 154A. Also keep expense receipts for internet, software, equipment, and other costs, though keeping them does not automatically mean you can claim a deduction, along with your NTN, filed returns, acknowledgement or submission records, wealth statements, PSEB certificate, and all FBR notices with your replies, attachments, receipts, and orders. Use a separate bank account for freelance income where possible, save organised digital copies with a backup, keep records accessible in Pakistan as Section 174 requires unless the Commissioner authorises otherwise, and do not share other people's CNICs, client information, or payment details publicly.
answer_ur: Apne tax records jis tax year se woh talluq rakhte hain us ke khatam hone ke baad chhe saal tak rakhein, aur kyunke Pakistan ka income-tax year 30 June ko khatam hota hai, Tax Year 2026 (1 July 2025 se 30 June 2026) ke records 30 June 2032 tak rakhein. Agar FBR ne aap ke khilaf koi proceeding, audit, appeal ya case shuru kiya ho to mutaliqa records us ke aakhri faisla tak rakhein, chahe chhe saal guzar jayein. Income ka saboot (invoices, client contracts, platform earning statements aur Upwork ya Fiverr records), freelance income wale har account ke mahana bank statements aur payment receipts, foreign payments ke records (PRCs ya e-PRCs, Payoneer ya Wise reports, aur currency, date, sender aur amount), aur khaas taur par Section 154A ke bank tax deduction certificates ya receipts rakhein. Internet, software, equipment jaise kharchon ki receipts bhi rakhein magar is se deduction khud ba khud claim nahi hota, aur NTN, filed returns, acknowledgement ya submission records, wealth statements, PSEB certificate, aur FBR ke notices, aapke jawab, attachments, receipts aur orders bhi rakhein. Mumkin ho to freelance income ke liye alag bank account rakhein, digital copies organise kar ke backup rakhein, Section 174 ke mutabiq jab tak Commissioner ijazat na de records Pakistan mein accessible rakhein, aur doosron ke CNIC, client information ya payment details publicly share na karein.
source_line: Based on FBR Income Tax Ordinance Section 174, FBR record-keeping guidance, and Supreme Court case summary (fbr.gov.pk). FBR helpline: 051 111 772 772
